To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of bilateral, peripheral, patchy groundglass opacifications with or without bronchiectasis and bronchial wall thickening, associated with a BAL lymphocytosis of 25% or more, are highly predictive of COP.

(i) in patients with a clinical diagnosis of COP, the combination of HRCT findings and the presence of a lymphocytic alveolitis with an increased CD4/CD8 ratio in BAL is highly suggestive of COP, and (ii) HRCT and BAL findings can be useful for the diagnosis of COP in patients with clinical suspicion of COP in which the transbronchial lung biopsy is negative or in whom a confirmatory lung biopsy cannot be performed.

(a) HRCT findings of COP were present in 100% of patients with a clinical diagnosis of COP, and (b) the presence of HRCT findings of organizing pneumonia in patients with a clinical presentation consistent with COP, and a negative transbronchial lung biopsy, is associated with a diagnosis of COP with a high probability.
